column1: # Phrases that are not a report on any kind of product (rules pc4). Columns, TABS: term | label | unless | reason | when

column4: fast battery drain is mostly not a complaint worth flagging; the team labels it quality only 1 in 11 times

a bare 'mabilis malowbat' is a remark, not a defect; abrupt or measurable wording (minutes, 'kahit full', 'agad', a number, 'isang gamit', a power bank) is a functional failure and stays flagged (policy B); the leading * makes these cues count when they sit inside the phrase itself, not only beside it

a negated drain ('hindi agad malowbat', 'hindi sya lowbat agad', 'di nalolowbat agad') says the battery does NOT run down: praise, not a failure, whatever abrupt wording ('agad') it carries. Only the unambiguous negators hindi/hinde/hnd/di/never, right before the drain word: 'wala na lowbat' means the battery is already dead, and 'hindi umaabot ng 10 mins, lowbat agad' is a complaint, so neither is covered
burning calories or a burn test is not a fire hazard
what the product treats, not a reaction to it
'akala ko peke pero original pala': the reviewer feared a fake and found it genuine
